messages:
Maya: kicked off a small canary for FlashAttention v3 on the redwood-small serving pool (4 GPUs). Quick summary: long-seq (≈2k tokens) p50 down ~12%, throughput +9%. Short-seq (<=128 tokens) p95 up ~6% on the canary: looks like workspace padding + extra kernel churn on mixed-shape batches. Posting telemetry snippets and a couple sample logs below.

Raj: nice! can you paste the runtime config you used for the canary? curious about workspace pool sizing and fallback rules.

Maya: sure — config we pushed to the canary: 
```
kernel: flashattn_v3
fallback: flashattn_v2
workspace_pool: per_gpu
workspace_max_bytes: 1200000000
shape_bucket_thresholds: [128, 512, 2048]
autobalance: true
```

Devon: what triggers a fallback back to v2 in this rollout? OOM only or also heuristics?

Maya: fallback order: (1) allocation failure (OOM at workspace request), (2) kernel runtime error (non-recoverable from CUDA side), (3) explicit heuristic when predicted workspace > max and config `force_fallback_on_estimate=true`. In the canary we saw both (1) and (3) a few times when mixed small+long batches hit worst-case padding. sample log lines: 
```
[2026-02-11T14:03:22Z] INFO kernel_selector: try kernel flashattn_v3 for model=redwood-small, seq=64, batch=64
[2026-02-11T14:03:22Z] WARN kernel_allocator: requested 1342177280 bytes > workspace_max 1200000000 -> fallback flashattn_v2
[2026-02-11T14:03:22Z] ERROR flashattn_v3: kernel_launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS -> fallback flashattn_v2
```

Sophia: can we add tags in telemetry so we can split these by seq_len_bucket + batching mode? right now p95 lumps mixed-shape tails with long-seq perf. need histogram per (model, seq_bucket, batching_mode).

Maya: agreed — I added `seq_bucket` and `batch_mode` labels to the canary metrics. we already emit `kernel_variant` and `fallback_reason`. sample metric names we pushed: `runtime.latency_ms{model,seq_bucket,kernel_variant,batch_mode}`, `runtime.fallbacks_total{reason,kernel_variant}`.

Raj: do we have per-kernel memory estimate telemetry? would be great to correlate estimated workspace vs actual allocation + OOMs.

Maya: yes, added `kernel.estimated_workspace_bytes` (histogram) and `kernel.actual_workspace_bytes` (histogram). early look: estimates overshoot for short seqs in mixed batches because we pad to the bucket max. that explains the p95 tail.

Devon: suggestion: add a fast-path heuristic: if batch is mixed and >N% short seq, prefer v2 (lower workspace variance). We could gate it behind a rollout flag.

Maya: good call. I'll prototype `mixed_shape_heuristic.enabled=true` with threshold `mixed_shape_short_ratio=0.7`. canary will flip to measure impact.

Sophia: also want an opt-in per-model override in the rollout controller so product teams can pin specific models to v2 until we tune buckets.

Maya: will add `model_force_kernel: {"redwood-chat-small":"flashattn_v2"}` to the rollout config.

infra-bot: deploy job 2981 started for canary config update by Maya.

deploy-bot: canary: 4/4 nodes updated, health ok, 10% traffic diverted.

Raj: one more ask — can we log the kernel selection decision with a small reason code (e.g., EST_OVER, MIXED_SHAPE, LAUNCH_ERR) so we can easily filter logs? right now free-text messages are noisy.

Maya: yep will switch to structured reason codes. plan: land telemetry labels + structured fallback reasons this week, then run another 24h canary with `mixed_shape_heuristic` on.

Devon: thanks — if the p95 short-seq improves after heuristic, we can do a gradual rollout. if not, we may need to widen shape buckets or tweak workspace_max. :thumbsup:
